parts.text: Speaker one.

I work as a lifeguard at a swimming pool. I have to be at the pool at seven in the morning, and I mustn't leave my chair when people are swimming. We don't have to wear a uniform, but we must wear a whistle. I can't use my phone during work, but I can swim in my lunch break.
Speaker two.

I'm a chef in a small Italian restaurant. In the kitchen we have to wash our hands every half an hour, and we must wear a white hat. I don't have to work on Mondays, because the restaurant is closed. The hardest thing is that I can't sit down for ten hours!
Speaker three.

I'm a primary school teacher. I have to prepare lessons every evening, and I must be polite to parents. Children mustn't run in the corridors, so I have to watch them in the breaks. The good thing is that I don't have to work in the summer. We have long holidays.
Welcome to Blue Wave Café, Tom. Let me explain the rules. You have to arrive ten minutes before your shift, and you must wear the blue uniform.
Do I have to bring my own apron?
No, you don't have to. We give you one. But you mustn't use your phone in the kitchen. If you want to call someone, you can do it in your break.
How long is the break?
Thirty minutes. You can have a free lunch, but you can't take food home.
OK. And what about weekends?
You have to work every second Saturday, but you don't have to work on Sundays. Next week you will probably start at nine.
Great. I think I'll enjoy it.
Hi Anna, you look tired. What's the matter?
I didn't sleep well. I have an English speaking exam on Friday and I'm really nervous.
Oh, I understand. What are you worried about?
I always forget words when I speak, and my pronunciation isn't good.
Well, you should practise every day. Why don't you record yourself on your phone and listen to it?
That's a good idea. But I don't have much time. I have football training on Tuesday and Thursday.
You'd better not miss the training, you need sport. But you could study for ten minutes before bed.
OK. And what about sleep? Tonight I'm going to stay up and study.
No, don't do that! You shouldn't stay up late. Go to bed early, and try not to drink coffee.
You're right. Thanks, Max. Shall we practise together tomorrow after school?
Sure! Let's meet at four at the library.
Welcome to Teen Talk. Our first caller today is Kate. Kate, what's your problem?
Hello. My problem is that I'm always tired in the morning. I go to bed at midnight because I play computer games, and then I can't get up for school.
I see. Well, Kate, you should turn off your computer at ten o'clock. And don't play games in bed. Why don't you read a book instead?
I've tried, but I don't like reading.
Then listen to music or a podcast. And you'd better not drink cola in the evening, because it has a lot of sugar.
OK. Shall I put my phone in another room?
Good idea! That's the best advice today. Thank you for calling, Kate.
